## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

Two-juan *yǔlù* in *Xuzangjing* X70 n1391. Preface by Huáihǎi Yuánzhào 淮海元肇 (then abbot of Yùwángshān) dated Jǐngdìng *guǐhài* mid-spring (early 1263). Five abbacy records: Píngjiāng Dìnghuì 定慧, Wēnzhōu Yànshān Néngrén 鴈山能仁, Jiāngzhōu Dōnglín 東林, Qìngyuán Tàibáimíngshān Tiāntóng Jǐngdé 太白名山天童景德, and Ruìyánshān Kāishàn 瑞巖開善. Followed in juan 2 by *fǎyǔ*, *báyǔ*, *jìsòng*, *zàn fózǔ*, *zìzàn*, *xiǎo fóshì*, and the *xíngzhuàng*.

**Abstract**

Per DILA A009257 and the *xíng-zhuàng*: Liǎo-huì (*hào* Xī-yán 西巖 "Western Cliff"), surname Luó 羅, native of Péng-chí 蓬池 in Péng-zhōu 蓬州 (Shǔ). Tonsured at nineteen by Zǔ-dēng 祖燈 of Ān-guó-sì on Yù-zhǎng-shān; studied briefly the *Prajñāpāramitā* *niàn-fó sān-mèi* (not to his taste), then the *xìng-zōng* sūtra scholarship at Chéngdū. He eventually trained across a striking range of masters: Huài-ān Zhào 壞菴照 at Zhāo-jué, Zhè-wēng Rú-yǎn 浙翁如琰, Gāo-yuán Zǔ-quán 高原祖泉, Wújùn Shīfàn 無準師範 (his transmission-master), Shí-tián Fǎ-xūn 石田法薰, and Miào-fēng Zhī-shàn 妙峰之善. Five successive abbacies, ending at Tiān-tóng, after which he retired to the Huàn-zhì-ān 幻智庵; died at 65 with 47 summer-retreats to his credit. Principal dharma-heirs: Dōng-yán Jìng-rì 東巖淨日 and Yuè-jiàn Wén-míng 月磵文明 (author of [KR6q0325](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0325)).
